corrected_value.title: Cognitive style and religiosity: The role of conflict detection.

decisions.location: Results / Discussion / References (ref 11), line 1 and line 12
decisions.quote: Indeed, when participants completed the analytic thinking task first we found significant negative correlations between NFC and intrinsic religiosity, r (205) = -.18, p = .011, and NFC and belief in supernatural agents, r (205) = -.17, p = .017, respectively, and a non-significant negative correlation between NFC and intuitive religious beliefs, r (205) = -.12, p = .080. These patterns mirror findings reported by Pennycook et al. (Study 1) [ 11 ]. When participants completed the religious beliefs measures first, however, NFC was no longer correlated with any of the religious beliefs measures: intrinsic religiosity r (205) = .06, p = .394; intuitive religious beliefs r (205) = .06, p = .384; belief in supernatural agents r (205) = .03, p = .647.

(2013, Study 1, reference [11]), stating that when participants completed the analytic thinking task first, 'These patterns mirror findings reported by Pennycook et al. (Study 1) [ 11 ].'
